Layout Lab

How the person’s day, activities, and workflows should be organized.

Explored5 directions

From timeline to flow hierarchy

The lab compared chronological rhythm, activity scanning, workflow sections, workflow-plus-inventory, and flow hierarchy.

QuestionShould the page follow a day, a list of activities, or the outcomes the person is trying to produce?
Useful insightA person can have multiple workflows of each type; foundational, supporting, and edge-case describe flow importance, not a one-to-one taxonomy.
Chosen · Option EApplied

Flow hierarchy

Separate foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows, then open each flow to see its embedded activity inventory.

What it preservesCadence, tools, what the person cares about most, friction, and the difference between normal work and recovery work.
Applied toPersona cards and detail views, with the workflow tiers kept inside each person.

Skill Layout Lab

How to show the capabilities behind the activities without losing the ability to scan.

Explored6 directions

From cards to context

The lab compared skill cards, a workflow matrix, a proficiency ladder, an expanded profile, skills inside flows, and a combined index-plus-detail view.

QuestionCan someone see the complete set of capabilities and still understand one skill deeply?
Useful insightThe top level needs a scan-friendly index; depth belongs in the selected skill rather than in a long wall of content.
Chosen · Option FApplied

Skill index + deep dive

Keep the complete Skills needed list visible, then select one capability to inspect its detail.

Deep dive includesDefinition, potential triggers, related workflows, observable actions, and evidence or validation detail.
Applied toThe persona detail page and the $persona-skills presentation guidance.

Decision trail

The sequence that shaped the current information architecture.

Research model

Activities stay close to their tools

Research output was expanded from role descriptions into activities, workflows, tools, skills, and sources.

Flow model

Work is separated by importance

Foundational, supporting, and edge-case flows became the organizing hierarchy, with multiple flows allowed in each tier.

Capability model

Skills become selectable profiles

Option F combines the scan of a list with the depth of a profile, while potential triggers explain when a capability becomes relevant.

Current state

Keep evidence and resources visible

The persona page keeps evidence status in the detail view and cited Resources at the very end.

Future capability backlog

Good ideas intentionally parked for a later build, with the reason and shape preserved here.

ParkedExploration

Full skill network map

Show multi-hop relationships between primitive capabilities, composed skills, workflows, and personas.

Why laterThe focused map is enough for reference; a global graph needs filtering and navigation rules first.
NotesConsider neighborhood depth, relationship filters, and a list view that remains usable with keyboard and assistive technology.
ParkedAuthoring

Skill composition editor

Let a maintainer assemble composed skills from existing primitives and connect them with typed relationships.

Why laterEditing relationships safely requires stronger validation, permissions, and versioning than the static library needs today.
NotesStart with “reuse existing unit” suggestions, duplicate and cycle checks, and an explicit rationale for each new connection.
ParkedAssessment

Skill coverage and assessment

Show which skills are well evidenced, thinly evidenced, or missing across personas and workflows.

Why laterCoverage metrics should wait until more personas and skill applications have been researched consistently.
NotesPotential views include evidence confidence, workflow coverage, proficiency signals, and validation gaps.
ParkedImpact

Dependency-aware version history

Show what downstream personas, workflows, and composed skills are affected when a primitive changes.

Why laterThis becomes valuable when the relationship graph has enough real reuse to create meaningful change impact.
NotesPair relationship diffs with reconciliation prompts and a review queue before allowing changes to propagate.

Still to validate

The structure is chosen; the next questions are about evidence quality and coverage.

  • Expand skill profiles for the other personas.
  • Validate synthesized triggers through interviews, observation, or work samples.
  • Keep source additions attached to the claims they support.

Open the working surfaces

Return to the prototypes whenever a new persona or evidence source challenges the current shape.
